quote: And reason for calling. I'll see if this person is available.
stewart_read: The call is screened by a third party before reaching Shirley, and the eventual respondent turns out to be 'Heather' rather than Shirley — this could reflect messy lead/household data or a call-screening handoff rather than rep error, but the rep never re-establishes who they are actually speaking to before pitching.
alternative_hypothesis: The confusion is entirely the rep's fault for not confirming identity clearly.
coaching_implication: When a call is screened and handed off, the rep should explicitly re-confirm who they're speaking to and their relationship to the lead name before proceeding — this is a data-hygiene and call-opening discipline gap, not necessarily a rep scripting failure.

stewart_read: The person answering confirms she is 'Shirley' after being addressed as Shirley at 00:42, yet the customer had identified herself as 'Heather' just two seconds earlier at 00:40 — an unresolved identity mismatch that neither party clarifies.
alternative_hypothesis: This could simply be a transcription/diarization artifact rather than a real customer inconsistency.
coaching_implication: Flag for QA — if this is a real identity mismatch, the account record needs correcting before this lead is worked again; the rep should not have proceeded with the pitch without resolving the name discrepancy.

quote: No. I didn't fill out any solar form.
stewart_read: The customer denies the lead source that legitimizes the call outright, and the rep's intro leans entirely on the form-fill framing with no state or Tesla-referral anchor as backup.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have accurately quoted the lead source and the customer simply forgot filling out a form months prior.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to have a second legitimacy anchor ready (e.g., specific address, referral source, date of inquiry) before the customer denies the first one — here the rep does recover with an address at 01:04, which is the right instinct.

quote: a little weird here. I got I got a request for 20 Mount Washington Drive for Shirley. Is that?
stewart_read: Facing an outright denial of the lead source, the rep pivots to a specific, verifiable address to re-establish credibility rather than arguing or dropping the call — an honest-specificity move that partially works, since the customer confirms the address is hers.
coaching_implication: This recovery move is worth reinforcing as a good instinct — leading with a specific, checkable detail defuses suspicion better than repeating a vague claim.

quote: And you're I mean, you're totally right. Solar in the past, I mean, it hasn't made a whole lot of sense.
stewart_read: The customer's 25-year payback complaint is a textbook objection_inversion trigger — the exact financial pain that justifies solar (a bad ROI, a big loan, out-of-pocket cost) could be flipped into 'that's exactly the old model we replaced' framing. The rep validates the complaint and gestures at a 'new program' but never anchors the flip to the customer's own numbers or pain.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep is strategically avoiding re-litigating a sore financial memory and choosing a soft, agreeable bridge instead.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the customer's own story more directly: reflect the 25-year and out-of-pocket numbers back as the very problem this new program was built to fix, rather than a general 'it hasn't made a whole lot of sense' statement.

stewart_read: This is not the first-30-seconds hello-objection scenario, so the applicable schema move is the changed_mind/curiosity-creation rebuttal (e.g., asking if she's seen the actual numbers for her home specifically) rather than accepting the refusal at face value.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged further pushing was pointless given two consecutive flat refusals and limited rapport built.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to deploy the curiosity_creation strategy here — ask a specific, low-pressure question tied to her own situation rather than echoing her objection back to her, which reads as capitulation rather than persistence.

stewart_read: The call ends with a passive sign-off and no attempt at a callback, alternative touchpoint, or even confirming whether Ion should follow up later — full disengagement with no next-step ownership.
coaching_implication: Even on a clear decline, the rep should leave a door open (e.g., 'no worries, if your situation changes, is it okay if we check back') rather than closing with a bare pleasantry.
